The Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ Patiently Bear the Loss of Sight
Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) Exercises Patience when he Loses his Sight

Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) says, "When I developed a cataract, Nabi ﷺ came to visit me. He asked, 'O Zaid! What would you do if you lost your eye?' 'I shall exercise patience and look forward to the rewards (from Allaah),' I replied. Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, 'If after losing your eye you exercise patience and anticipate the rewards, your reward will be Jannah.'"[^2]

Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that he accompanied Rasulullaah ﷺ to visit Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) when he was suffering from an eye ailment. Rasulullaah ﷺ said to him, "O Zaid! If you lose your eye and exercise patience and anticipate the rewards, you will meet Allaah without a single sin against your name."[^3]

Hadhrat Zaid bin Arqam (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once visited him when he was ill. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "No harm will come to you from this illness but what will you do if you reach old age after my demise and then lose your eyesight?" Hadhrat Zaid (RA) replied, "I shall then exercise patience and anticipate the rewards." "In that case," Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked, "you shall enter Jannah without reckoning." Hadhrat Zaid (RA) later did go blind after Rasulullaah ﷺ's demise.[^4] Another narration adds that after the demise of Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Zaid (RA) did go blind but Allaah restored his eyesight before he passed away. May Allaah shower his mercies on him.[^5]
A Sahabi (RA) Exercises Patience upon the Loss of his Eyesight

Hadhrat Qaasim bin Muhammad narrates that when some people visited a Sahabi (RA) who had lost his eyesight, he said, "I wanted my sight only to see Rasulullaah ﷺ. However, since Rasulullaah ﷺ has passed away, it would not even please me to use them to see a gazelle from the gazelles of Tabaala (a place in Yemen)."[^6]
